obligation.description: If another configured voter has actually won a newer-term majority election before VerifyLeader is invoked on L, and L does not reacquire authority during that operation, completed VerifyLeader must not return success based solely on a held reply produced before that election.

scope.description: Bounded verification API result after same-history replacement election; initial static leader/configuration fixture and controlled worker scheduling.

Crash-only delays/partition; no forged vote or heartbeat response.
No L reacquisition or configuration changes during the operation.

grounding.derivation: VerifyLeader is specified to ensure the peer is still leader and prevent stale data after leadership loss. Under a static three-voter configuration, actual election of F in term 8 by its own vote and N vote before invocation means L in term 7 cannot validly confirm continued authority during this operation absent reacquisition. Therefore a completed verification on L must not report success solely on an earlier term-7 reply. This is a necessary negative condition in the observed replacement-election context, not a requirement for all replies to be fresh or for verification eventually to complete.
grounding.applicability: Fixed voters L,F,N; pre-vote disabled for the replacement election; no L reelection, configuration change or newer reply during the verification interval; delayed genuine F response.

materials.text:
r.mainThreadSaturation.sleeping()

		select {
		case rpc := <-r.rpcCh:
			r.mainThreadSaturation.working()
			r.processRPC(rpc)

		case <-r.leaderState.stepDown:
			r.mainThreadSaturation.working()
			r.setState(Follower)

### Leader Write

Most write operations must be performed on the leader.

* RequestConfigChange - update the raft peer list configuration
* Apply - apply a log entry to the log on a majority of peers, and the FSM. See [raft apply](apply.md) for more details.
* Barrier - a special Apply that does not modify the FSM, used to wait for previous logs to be applied
* LeadershipTransfer - stop accepting client requests, and tell a different peer to start a leadership election
* Restore (Snapshot) - overwrite the cluster state with the contents of the snapshot (excluding cluster configuration)
* VerifyLeader - send a heartbeat to all voters to confirm the peer is still the leader

grounding.derivation: VerifyLeader is specified to ensure the peer is still leader and prevent stale data after leadership loss. Under a static three-voter configuration, actual election of F in term 8 by its own vote and N vote before invocation means L in term 7 cannot validly confirm continued authority during this operation absent reacquisition. Therefore a completed verification on L must not report success solely on an earlier term-7 reply. This is a necessary negative condition in the observed replacement-election context, not a requirement for all replies to be fresh or for verification eventually to complete.

r.mainThreadSaturation.sleeping()

		select {
		case rpc := <-r.rpcCh:
			r.mainThreadSaturation.working()
			r.processRPC(rpc)

		case <-r.leaderState.stepDown:
			r.mainThreadSaturation.working()
			r.setState(Follower)

### Leader Write

Most write operations must be performed on the leader.

* RequestConfigChange - update the raft peer list configuration
* Apply - apply a log entry to the log on a majority of peers, and the FSM. See [raft apply](apply.md) for more details.
* Barrier - a special Apply that does not modify the FSM, used to wait for previous logs to be applied
* LeadershipTransfer - stop accepting client requests, and tell a different peer to start a leadership election
* Restore (Snapshot) - overwrite the cluster state with the contents of the snapshot (excluding cluster configuration)
* VerifyLeader - send a heartbeat to all voters to confirm the peer is still the leader
